text.p: The research arm of Germany's Vereinsbank AG said on Monday it had upped its recommendation on shares in packaging-maker Schmalbach-Lubeca AG to above-average from market neutral.
Vereinsbank said it had raised its earnings per share (EPS) forecasts for 1997 to 25 marks per share, up from 23 marks, after 18 marks per share in 1996.

For 1998 Vereinsbank analysts were forecasting EPS of 31 marks, and said the share would register above-average performance compared to the MDAX index of medium-sized stocks, even after a good run on the index of late.

Vereinsbank said the sale of the firm's plastics unit to the British firm RPG Group, the purchase of Johnson Controls' PET business and the merger of its metal packaging unit with France's Pechiney were the main factors behind increased yields and the improved market position for Schmalbach-Lubeca.
From 1997 onwards, the group would be hit by tight margins in the metal packaging sector and in plastics, Vereinsbank said.
Schmalbach-Lubeca ended bourse trade on Monday down six marks at 384 marks.
